source_note: European wholesale gas (TTF) prices spiked roughly 4-5x pre-war levels by mid-2022; figure approximates household energy bill impact, illustrative not exact.
Germany's 2022 annual inflation reached its highest level in decades, widely reported around 8-9% YoY, driven substantially by energy costs.
Brent crude jumped roughly 3-4% the day after the strike, then eased within weeks as the crisis did not escalate further.
The Korean won depreciated against the US dollar over 2018 amid broader trade-war/EM pressure; multiple factors contributed, not solely the trade war.
US retail gasoline prices rose about 40% in November 1973 alone, during the OAPEC embargo.
US annual inflation rose from 3.3% (1972) to 11% (1974), driven substantially by the oil shock.
Germany's inflation rose more mildly than the US, from 5.5% (1972) to 7% (1973) - a much smaller jump despite the same global shock.
Japan's inflation spiked severely, from 4.8% (1972) to 23% (1974) - among the most severe of major economies, reflecting Japan's heavy oil import dependency at the time.
